newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINLAND JOBLESS MEASURES DIVERGE ON SUMMER JOBS - SF.
newsitem.headline: FINLAND JOBLESS MEASURES DIVERGE ON SUMMER JOBS - SF.

text.p: Different measuring methods for summer job applicants caused a move in opposite directions in Finland's June jobless rate between Statistics Finland (SF) and the labour ministry, an SF official said on Thursday.
SF earlier said the June unemployment rate fell to 15 percent from 16.7 percent in May, while the labour ministry last week reported an increase to 16.5 percent from 15.5 percent.
"The main reason is that our measure catches students who seek summer jobs already in May, while in June many are already working," said SF reasearcher Paivi Keinanen.
In May, this caused SF's jobless rate to rise, while the labour ministry's May jobless rate fell, she noted.
